summary: Streaming alignment. Host: live_text publishes at every whitespace (token) boundary instead of every newline, still redacting the whole publishable prefix so a partial word is never released before its redactor sees it (PEM/assignment/header/bearer tests unchanged and green at every split). subscription.rs turns each live text in an emitted view (project desktop_stream_text, prompt_statuses[].stream_text, worker_statuses[].stream_text) into an ordered delta {<prefix>_offset, <prefix>_delta}: offset = Unicode scalar values the client keeps from the text this subscription last sent for that stream, delta = appended suffix. Within a subscription every new token is a pure append (offset == held length); a TextDone/redaction rewrite resends only the changed suffix; a new subscription (reconnect) restarts every stream at offset 0 so replay replaces instead of doubling; streams absent from a view are forgotten on both sides. Android SubscriptionReducer rebuilds stream_text from the held projection before the unchanged codecs run, and refuses full texts on a subscription, offsets past the held text (gap), non-integer/negative offsets and half-present delta pairs, leaving the projection untouched.

notes: Deviations / decisions: (1) The blueprint's owned path android/.../state/SubscriptionReducer.kt does not exist; the reducer lives in android/.../transport/SubscriptionReducer.kt, which is what was changed. (2) Tests outside the owned paths: tests/remote_live_text.rs, tests/remote_subscription.rs, tests/remote_android_interop.rs (new #[ignore] interop test, picked up by tools/build_android_interop_classes.sh --run in CI), android SubscriptionTest.kt (fixtures moved from full texts to the delta form) and new AndroidRustStreamTest.kt. (3) 'Token' = whitespace-delimited token: provider deltas are re-cut at whitespace so a credential word is only released whole and redacted; finer cuts would publish partial secrets. (4) The 4 KiB per-stream cap (MAX_LIVE_TEXT_BYTES) is kept on purpose: one-shot WorkspaceList responses still carry full texts for up to 16 prompts plus worker/desktop streams inside the 256 KiB control frame, and Android's codecs validate the same 4096-byte bound; with deltas a subscription no longer resends the preview on every change. (5) Offsets count Unicode scalar values (Rust chars == Kotlin code points), independent of UTF-8/UTF-16 width. (6) Non-subscription responses (WorkspaceList, worker pages) keep full stream_text as their snapshot; the subscription view is the only incremental channel. No protocol version bump: subscription_view content is host-defined and both sides ship together.
